verdict.rationale: Stripe Issuing's spending controls document blocking merchant categories and merchant IDs, so the MCC blocklist half of the story is covered. The evidence does not show MCC allowlists or single-merchant locks. The real-time authorization webhook is a developer building block for custom approve/decline logic, so it earns no credit toward those controls. Missing for 10: documented MCC allowlists, single-merchant lock capability, explicit confirmation that the controls are enforced at authorization time, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can restrict where a card works — merchant category (MCC) allowlists and blocklists, and single-merchant locks — applied at authorization time

citations.quote: You can use spending controls to block merchant categories (for example, bakeries), countries, merchant IDs, or card presence
